roadmap_events.goal: Revise BA 815 for 2026: same statistical backbone, AI woven throughout, oral exams replace quizzes, a 20% project, R/Python/Excel tool tracks, refreshed examples.

steps.name: Ground truth
steps.done_when: The old weight table, session and quiz count, and deck inventory are extracted from the BA 815 folder and checked against your stated 20/10/10 delta.
oranges_annotations: Your delta is stated against a table recalled from memory — if the real table differs, the syllabus math changes before anything is drafted.
The quiz count in the old structure fixes the oral-exam seat count for everything downstream.

steps.name: Assessment & policy decisions
steps.done_when: Weights locked; project shape (milestones vs one end deliverable) decided; tool-track model (student choice vs three tracks) decided; AI-use policy written; Smeal/recording sign-off status known.
oranges_annotations: The tool-track choice is the cheapest decision with the biggest multiplier: student-choice is 1× homework authoring, three tracks is 3×.
Chair sign-off has a queue — asking now costs nothing; asking in August costs the syllabus.

steps.name: Syllabus 2026
steps.done_when: A submission-ready syllabus exists that a reviewer at Smeal could approve without rewriting the oral-exam or AI language.
oranges_annotations: The syllabus is the contract: everything downstream quotes it, so a late weight or policy change ripples through every deck.
Oral-exam wording must survive recording-consent and accommodation review, not just read well.

steps.name: Oral exam engine
steps.done_when: One quiz oral has been piloted end-to-end — AI conducts it, transcript and rubric produced, appeal path decided.
oranges_annotations: Two formats hide in here — recurring quiz check and project defense — with different lengths, rubrics, and prompts; build the short one first.
Decide AI-grades versus AI-interviews-and-you-grade before the first real run: at 150+ runs, hand-grading becomes the bottleneck.
The first disputed grade will test the appeal path, so it must exist before it is needed.

steps.name: Session 1 package
steps.done_when: Orientation deck, Professor Liechty intro deck, and lecture 1 (data types, sampling, inference, new running example, AI demo and student AI-experience pulse) are done and consistent with the syllabus.
oranges_annotations: Choose the COVID replacement to be reusable across the whole term — one running dataset compounds; a one-off example is spent in week 1.
The week-1 AI-experience pulse calibrates how fast you can push the AI thread all semester — design it to be comparable, not just conversational.

steps.name: Term rebuild
steps.done_when: Sessions 2–N refreshed with AI integrated, homework re-authored per the tool-track decision, project brief and defense rubric issued, and one dry-run consistency pass over the whole package.
oranges_annotations: This is the bulk of the hours, and it scales directly with the stage-2 tool decision made months earlier.
If homework datasets and the project dataset are chosen together, project work rehearses homework skills instead of competing with them.

roadmap_events.goal: Revise BA 815 for 2026: same statistical backbone, AI integrated throughout, quizzes as AI-run oral exams, R/Python/Excel tool track, new project, refreshed examples.

steps.name: Ground truth
steps.done_when: Old weight table, session and lecture count, quiz count and timing, and deck inventory extracted from the BA 815 folder; the 20/10/10 delta and your four-lectures-per-block assumption checked against what the old course actually did.
oranges_annotations: Your block plan assumes three quizzes and roughly four lectures per block — if the old course's session map disagrees, the whole quiz cadence shifts, so verify before the syllabus prints dates.

steps.name: Assessment & policy decisions
steps.done_when: Weights locked; project shape (milestones vs one end deliverable) decided; tool-track model (student choice vs three tracks) decided; AI-use policy written; recording and accommodation sign-off status known.
oranges_annotations: The tool-track decision is the 1x-vs-3x multiplier on every homework in stage 4 — it is the single most expensive open question in the campaign.
The milestone decision decides whether defenses and final grading pile into the last two weeks or spread across the term.

steps.name: Syllabus 2026
steps.done_when: A submission-ready syllabus a Smeal reviewer could approve without rewriting the oral-exam or AI language.
oranges_annotations: The syllabus publishes quiz dates and homework counts before any block is rebuilt — once students have it, renumbering a quiz is an announced amendment, so keep dates as 'week of' unless you are sure.

steps.name: Homework model & sets
steps.done_when: The homework format under AI is defined — what is graded when an agent can do the mechanics — and sets are re-authored per the tool-track decision.
oranges_annotations: An AI agent solves a traditional problem set in one shot; if the graded artifact stays 'the answer,' every homework is already broken — the format has to grade the analysis conversation, not the number.
Homework leans on lecture examples you have not refreshed yet — sets authored here will need a re-sync pass as blocks 1–3 change the examples, unless authoring moves inside each block.

steps.name: Project spec
steps.done_when: Project brief, grading rubric, milestone schedule if staged, and oral-defense format issued in student-facing form.
oranges_annotations: If students pick their own datasets, approving 30 team datasets that can actually support a GLM analysis becomes a hidden weekly task — a curated data menu is cheaper.
The defense rubric and the quiz-oral rubric will share the same engine — write them together or they drift apart.

steps.name: Oral exam engine
steps.done_when: One quiz oral piloted end-to-end — AI conducts it, transcript and rubric produced, appeal and accommodation paths decided.
oranges_annotations: Pilot with real audio, not text — accents, crosstalk, and dropped connections are the failure modes, and a flagged transcript is cheap in a pilot but a grade dispute in week 5.
The accommodation alternative (extended time, non-audio format) must exist before quiz 1, not be improvised after the first request arrives.

steps.name: Block 1 + Quiz 1
steps.done_when: Orientation deck, Professor Liechty intro deck, and the first block of lectures rebuilt — data types, sampling, inference, a new running example replacing COVID, AI demo and student AI-experience pulse — and quiz 1 redone as an oral on the engine.
oranges_annotations: Session 1 carries triple weight — orientation, intro, and lecture — and the running example you choose here has to survive all three blocks, so pick it with blocks 2 and 3 in mind.
This block sets the AI-integration template every later lecture copies; over-engineer it here and you pay nine more times.

steps.name: Block 2 + Quiz 2
steps.done_when: The second block of lectures rebuilt with AI integrated and examples refreshed; quiz 2 redone; template adjustments from block 1 folded in.
oranges_annotations: By now block 1 has met real students in your head if not in a classroom — this is the last cheap point to change the lecture template before it is baked into the remaining half of the course.

steps.name: Block 3 + Quiz 3 & close-out
steps.done_when: The final block of lectures rebuilt; quiz 3 redone; one dry-run consistency pass over syllabus, homework, project spec, and all decks as a single package.
oranges_annotations: This is where everything converges — quiz 3, project defenses, final grading in the same two weeks — and the milestone decision from stage 2 either saved you here or didn't.
The consistency pass is not optional polish: nine stages of edits guarantee the syllabus, decks, and homework disagree somewhere by now.

What decision, if any, requires a human gate?

roadmap_events.goal: Revise BA 815 for 2026: keep the statistical backbone and structure, integrate AI throughout, replace quizzes with AI-run oral exams, open the tool track to R/Python/Excel, add a course project, refresh the examples.

steps.name: Deep read of the drop (Gandalf heavy)
steps.done_when: Gandalf heavy verdict on everything dropped into the project — BA 815 decks, the NYU Stern oral-exam material, symposium notes — saying what the course actually is and how the material is organized; the old weight table, session/lecture/quiz counts, and deck inventory extracted as hard numbers; unclear or missing material flagged.
oranges_annotations: This run absorbs the old ground-truth stage: if it returns judgment without the hard numbers — weights, session count, quiz timing — the decisions stage stalls and you pay for a second extraction pass.
The drop is more than BA 815: the run should sort what is course source, what is engine reference (the NYU oral-exam material), and what is background, or every later stage re-litigates that.

steps.name: External scan (researchPrime)
steps.done_when: A filtered brief on outside material worth using: how others run AI-conducted oral exams, AI-integrated statistics courses, and candidate running examples to replace COVID — each item tagged adopt, adapt, or ignore.
oranges_annotations: Unaimed research returns a pile; the shopping list is Gandalf's gap list plus three named needs — an oral-exam precedent beyond what you already hold, AI-in-stats course models, a replacement running example.
Anything adopted here hardens fast: an outside dataset or exam protocol that reaches the syllabus becomes contract language — swapping it after that means reprinting the contract.

steps.name: Assessment & policy decisions
steps.done_when: Weights locked; project shape (milestones vs one end deliverable) decided; tool-track model (student choice vs three tracks) decided; AI-use policy written; recording and accommodation sign-off status known.
oranges_annotations: Weights are half-locked already (project 20%, participation gone, homework down 10) — verify them against the extracted table before they become syllabus text.
The tool-track call is the 1× vs 3× multiplier on every homework set authored after this point.
With participation deleted, no discretionary component absorbs a disputed AI-graded oral — decide here whether 5% instructor judgment survives.

steps.name: Syllabus 2026
steps.done_when: A submission-ready syllabus a Smeal reviewer could approve without rewriting the oral-exam or AI language.
oranges_annotations: The oral-exam and AI-use paragraphs are the part a reviewer rewrites; if dean/chair sign-off status is still unknown when this ships, it ships twice.

steps.name: Homework model & sets
steps.done_when: The homework format under AI is defined — what is graded when an agent can do the mechanics — and sets are re-authored per the tool-track decision.
oranges_annotations: The format question is the real work: grading effort and reasoning, not output an agent produces for free — the problems are secondary to that decision.
Authoring every set up front means re-syncing them when blocks 1–3 refresh the examples; define the format here and expect per-block edits.

steps.name: Project spec
steps.done_when: Project brief, grading rubric, milestone schedule if staged, and oral-defense format issued in student-facing form.
oranges_annotations: If the defense lands only at term end, 30 defenses plus final grading plus the last quiz oral stack into the final two weeks — the milestone decision from the decisions stage is what spreads that.

steps.name: Oral exam engine
steps.done_when: One quiz oral piloted end-to-end — AI conducts it, transcript and rubric produced, appeal and accommodation paths decided.
oranges_annotations: Two formats share this engine — the short quiz oral and the long project defense — same plumbing, different rubrics and lengths; build for both now or retrofit later.
A disputed grade is defended with a transcript; appeal and accommodation paths are engine features, not policy afterthoughts.

steps.name: Block 1 + Quiz 1
steps.done_when: Orientation deck, Professor Liechty intro deck, and the first block of lectures rebuilt — data types, sampling, inference, a new running example replacing COVID, AI demo and student AI-experience pulse — and quiz 1 redone as an oral on the engine.
oranges_annotations: This block sets the template — running example, AI-demo pattern, deck skeleton — that blocks 2 and 3 inherit; an hour of template care here saves a rebuild there.
Quiz 1 is the engine's first live contact with students; leave slack for what the pilot didn't catch.

steps.name: Block 2 + Quiz 2
steps.done_when: The second block of lectures rebuilt with AI integrated and examples refreshed; quiz 2 redone; template adjustments from block 1 folded in.
oranges_annotations: Fold block-1 template fixes in before authoring this block, not after — retrofitting two finished blocks doubles the churn.

steps.name: Block 3 + Quiz 3 & close-out
steps.done_when: The final block of lectures rebuilt; quiz 3 redone; one dry-run consistency pass over syllabus, homework, project spec, and all decks as a single package.
oranges_annotations: The close-out pass is where syllabus promises meet what got built — any example or tool language the blocks changed must be reconciled against the contract shipped in the syllabus stage.

steps.name: Deep read of the drop (Gandalf heavy)
steps.done_when: Gandalf heavy verdict on the full drop — BA 815 decks, the Stern oral-exam material, symposium notes — saying what the course actually is and how the material is organized; the old weight table, session/lecture/quiz counts, and deck inventory extracted as hard numbers; unclear or missing material flagged as a concrete gap list that aims the researchPrime sweep.
oranges_annotations: The drop holds duplicates — the Stern zip beside its unzipped folder, the symposium summary as both docx and PDF. Canonical copies get declared before the read, or the verdict double-counts and the deck inventory inflates.

Gandalf should date-stamp what it reads: if the folder mixes semesters, the 'old course' it describes is a blend of two years, and the quiz timing it extracts will quietly contradict the three-block tail of the roadmap.
The gap list is a deliverable, not a by-product — it is the only aim the researchPrime sweep gets. Vague gaps mean the sweep re-finds the Stern material you already own.
